Subject: Request: credits for KeeperFest maintainers + ops plan

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. KeeperFest is running our winter maintainer sprint (Dec 4–10) and we’re coordinating compute/credits for 18 participating maintainers across 5 projects. Typical ask: enough inference credits for each maintainer to run local tests, CI runs, and a short demo evaluation — roughly 250k tokens per maintainer (conservative estimate).

What we need from Redwood:
- One-time promo credit pool that admins can distribute (no per-user billing)
- A 6-week trial extension window for invited accounts (Dec 1 – Jan 15)
- Simple onboarding link and a short FAQ for maintainers with quota guidance

Attachments: application doc (see attached) and last sprint report.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful — we’re on a tight timeline to finalize logistics by Nov 25.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Operations Lead, KeeperFest
sofia@keeperfest.org

They need logistics locked by Nov 25. If it helps I can approve a modest grant from my discretionary community fund but want to align with CS + Engineering.

- Grant total promo pool equivalent to 5,000,000 tokens (we can translate to USD-equivalent for accounting — I’ll work with finance).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: credits for KeeperFest maintainers + ops plan

Thanks — technical notes from infra: 5M tokens as a pool looks fine. A few operational guardrails I recommend:

- Model family restriction: prefer to allocate for the 'redwood-base' and 'redwood-chat' families only for this promo to keep costs predictable.
- Per-account cap: set soft cap 300k tokens/account and hard cap 350k to give a small buffer for debugging (this matches Sofia’s estimate and keeps margin).
- Rate limiting: 5 requests/sec per account, burst to 15/sec for 60s allowed.
- Quota provisioning: ops team can create a promo code tied to a single internal bucket; we’ll implement auto-shutdown if spend rate exceeds 70% of expected trajectory.

I’ll add these constraints to the promo configuration. If Ops needs a sandbox project to test onboarding flows we can spin one up tomorrow.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Hi Sofia —

Great news: Monica has approved a 5,000,000-token promo pool for KeeperFest; Karthik has confirmed the operational guardrails (model family restriction + per-account caps). Below are the next steps and what we’ll deliver this week:

1) Promo code + allocation: Ops will create a single promo code covering the 5M token pool. Code expires 2027-01-15.
2) Per-account controls: soft cap 300k / hard cap 350k; models limited to redwood-base / redwood-chat; rate limits applied as noted.
3) Onboarding: please send the maintainers list (emails) and a short FAQ/one-pager. We’ll provide an onboarding link and a short runbook for best practices (token budgeting tips + model selection).
4) Paperwork: I’ve attached the MOU template — if you can sign and return by Nov 25 we’ll queue finance for accounting. Also attaching a simple billing spreadsheet for bookkeeping.

Links: HubSpot record HS-Contact-54829; onboarding GDrive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xKeeperFestOnboarding

Attachment stubs: keeperfest_MOU.pdf (signed once KeeperFest confirms), keeperfest_billing_info.xlsx

If helpful I can also host a 20-minute onboarding AMA next week for maintainers. Let me know a preferred time.

Thanks and looking forward to the sprint —
